---
title: "Solution: GLMs — Logistic and Poisson Regression"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(nycflights13)
library(broom)
```

```{r prepare-data}
flights_clean <- flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>
  mutate(
    long_delay = as.integer(dep_delay > 30),
    hour       = as.numeric(hour),
    month      = as.numeric(month)
  )
```

## Task 1: Explore the binary outcome

```{r task1}
cat("Overall proportion with long delay (> 30 min):",
    round(mean(flights_clean$long_delay), 3), "\n")

hourly_delay <- flights_clean |>
  group_by(hour) |>
  summarise(
    prop_long = mean(long_delay),
    n         = n()
  )

ggplot(hourly_delay, aes(x = hour, y = prop_long)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(flights_clean$long_delay),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title    = "Proportion of flights with departure delay > 30 min, by hour",
    subtitle = "Orange dashed = overall mean. Evening flights are much more likely to be delayed.",
    x        = "Departure hour",
    y        = "Proportion with long delay"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 2: Fit the null and logistic models

```{r task2}
mod_null  <- glm(long_delay ~ 1,            family = binomial(), data = flights_clean)
mod_logit <- glm(long_delay ~ hour + month, family = binomial(), data = flights_clean)

summary(mod_logit)
```

## Task 3: Odds ratios

```{r task3}
or <- exp(coef(mod_logit))
print(round(or, 4))

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat("hour OR:", round(or["hour"], 3),
    "— each additional hour of the day multiplies\n",
    "   the odds of a long delay by", round(or["hour"], 3), "\n")
cat("   A flight at 18:00 vs 6:00 has odds ratio exp(",
    round(coef(mod_logit)["hour"], 3), " * 12) =",
    round(exp(coef(mod_logit)["hour"] * 12), 2),
    "times higher odds of a long delay.\n")
```

## Task 4: Predicted probability curve

```{r task4}
grid_hour <- data.frame(hour = 0:23, month = 7) |>
  add_predictions(mod_logit, type = "response")

ggplot(grid_hour, aes(x = hour, y = pred)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_point(colour = "darkorange", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(
    title    = "Logistic regression: P(departure delay > 30 min) vs hour",
    subtitle = "July flights (month = 7). Risk rises steadily through the day.",
    x        = "Departure hour",
    y        = "P(long delay)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 5: AIC comparison

```{r task5}
AIC(mod_null, mod_logit)

delta <- AIC(mod_null) - AIC(mod_logit)
cat("ΔAIC:", round(delta, 1), "\n")

# mod_logit has a substantially lower AIC (ΔAIC >> 10), confirming that
# hour and month meaningfully improve prediction of long delays.
# Despite this, the overall R²-equivalent (McFadden's pseudo-R²) is small
# because departure delays are largely unpredictable from scheduling info alone —
# weather and operational factors dominate.
```
